paragraphs: FlightBI sells aviation business intelligence to airports, helping their managers read flight distribution, demand growth, traffic origins and destinations, and traveler behavior. It sells to airlines as well, covering market size, demand growth, fare trends and the competitive landscape. Travel management companies are a third audience, using the analysis to read traveler preferences and behavior.

The products are sold as a suite for aviation decision making. One platform analyzes passenger origins at ZIP-code level and measures traffic leakage to competing airports. A separate catchment platform works at the census subdivision level for Canadian airports. A planning platform helps air service development teams find market opportunities and build airline proposals. A forecasting product predicts hourly passenger volumes up to seven days ahead for United States airports.

The company also offers a tool that answers aviation questions posed in ordinary language rather than through a data analyst. Customer comments on the site are attributed to air service development roles at airports that are described but not named.
